previous_description: Root container for an application's complete routing structure, composing all Route, NavigationTransition, and NavigationGuard nodes into a unified navigation model.
definition: A root container representing one application's complete router configuration, the single top-level route table or router instance whose scope covers every Route, NavigationTransition, NavigationGuard, NavigationFlow and BreadcrumbConfig reachable in that application. Exactly one exists per independently bootstrapped router, as opposed to a subset, journey or single entry.

distinguish_from.when: the symbol describes an ordered, goal-directed subset of routes, such as a wizard or checkout, rather than the whole route table of the application.
the symbol is a single path entry, including a parent route with nested children or a lazily loaded child route module, rather than the root router configuration.
the symbol only configures breadcrumb trail rendering for a navigation scope rather than defining the routes themselves.

standard_reference: SPA Navigation Patterns: root router configuration / route table (e.g., Vue Router createRouter instance, Angular RouterModule.forRoot, React Router createBrowserRouter)
code_evidence: A root router bootstrap call that receives the full routes array, such as createRouter({ history, routes }), RouterModule.forRoot(routes), createBrowserRouter([...]) or provideRouter(routes), which is mounted once on the app instance.
A top-level routing file, such as router/index.ts, app-routing.module.ts or routes.tsx, that imports and assembles all feature route modules and registers global guards like router.beforeEach.
The root directory of a file-system routing convention, such as Next.js app/ or pages/, Nuxt pages/ or SvelteKit src/routes, treated as one application's complete route tree.

attribute_descriptions.name: version
attribute_descriptions.description: Version identifier of this navigation model, such as a semver string matching the application release or route-table revision it reflects. Set it whenever the graph is extracted or published, so that changes to the routing structure can be tracked over time.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Free-text summary of the graph's scope: which application or router instance it covers and any notable boundaries, such as excluded micro-frontends or admin sub-apps. Set it when the scope is not obvious from the application reference.

notes: Both 'aggregates' and 'composes' relationships exist to Route and NavigationTransition, which is redundant; choose one. The meaning of 'version' is ambiguous: model revision or router library version. The router library belongs in the technology.systemsoftware link. Define the cardinality rule for micro-frontends or multiple router instances. Consider adding a 'routerFramework' or 'historyMode' attribute.
